title: Canary Safety Mosaic: Activation Stakeholder Matrix & De-escalation Playbook (WIP)
content:
WORK-IN-PROGRESS: high-level notes, activation matrix, and de-escalation scripts for cross-functional canaries and A/B rollouts. This doc is intentionally prescriptive and operational — meant to be used by product owners, SREs, on-call, and customer success during staged activations.

Purpose:
- Reduce ambiguity during small-batch activations for latency-sensitive LLM routes.
- Provide a short, actionable stakeholder matrix and runbook for rapid de-escalation.
- Surface telemetry primitives we rely on and a minimal checklist for safe exposure.

Context and constraints:
- Applies to model-serving changes (model variant swaps, prompt template changes, reranker updates) and routing policies that affect latency/cost.
- Target SLOs: p95 < 350ms for short-chat routes, p95 < 800ms for long-generation routes.
- Cost guardrail: token-unit spend delta > 20% vs baseline for sustained 10m window triggers a throttle.

Activation Stakeholder Matrix (who does what):
- Activation Lead (Product, single owner): coordinates experiment hypothesis, traffic slices, stakeholders, and final go/no-go.
- Runtime Steward (Serving / Infra): validates capacity, canary env readiness, and implements automated rollback hooks.
- Observability Lead (SRE/Telemetry): curates dashboards, synthesizes early signals, declares signal severity.
- Customer Success Rep: flags downstream customer anomalies and customer-facing messaging.
- Oncall Incident Lead: executes de-escalation, coordinates postmortem if needed.
- UX / Safety Reviewer (if behavioral changes): rapid manual review of 50 sampled outputs at 1% exposure.

Signal Catalog (primary + secondary):
Primary signals (auto-monitored):
- Latency p95 and p99 (route-level) — threshold breach: p95 increase > 150% vs baseline sustained for 5m.
- Error ratio (5xx, timeouts) — threshold: > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline for 3m.
- Token cost delta per request — threshold: +20% sustained 10m.
- Success-rate by cohort (A/B) — threshold: drop > 3 percentage points vs control for 30m.

Secondary signals (manual or aggregated):
- Semantic regression score on holdout prompts (daily regression > 2 std dev).
- Customer complaints matched to experiment cohort (2+ distinct customers within 60m).
- Manual review flags for toxicity or hallucination surface.

Automatic guard actions (what the system does):
- Soft throttle: reduce new-exposure weight by half when latency cost guard trips (automated rollback disabled).
- Canary pause: freeze further ramping and notify owners if primary signals breach.
- Fallback swap: automatically route affected traffic to last-stable model variant after error ratio threshold.

Human de-escalation playbook (ordered steps):
1) Detection: Observability Lead declares an incident-level signal (severity 1/2/3).
2) Immediate containment (first 5 minutes): Runtime Steward triggers canary pause or fallback swap (configurable).
3) Triage (5–20 minutes): Activation Lead + Observability Lead + Runtime Steward review metrics and recent commits/config changes.
4) Customer triage (20–45 minutes): Customer Success checks for customer impact, drafts inbound comms if >5 affected customers.
5) Remediation (45–90 minutes): if rollback required, Runtime Steward executes model swap and validates sanity metrics.
6) Post-action verification (next 30–60 minutes): Observability Lead confirms metrics returning to baseline; schedule postmortem.
7) Postmortem & learnings: within 72 hours, produce a concise incident note and decide changes to thresholds or automation.

Communication templates (short):
- Initial incident slack: "[ALERT] Canary exposure paused for <route>. Primary signal: latency p95 spike. Activation Lead: @name. Runtime Steward running fallback. Status: containment in progress"
- Customer-facing minimal: "We observed degraded responses for a subset of traffic and routed affected requests to a stable variant. If you see issues, contact support@redwood.ai with timestamp and request id."

Experiment gating heuristics (pre-launch checks):
- Minimum sample size: start at 0.5% traffic for high-risk changes (behavioral), 2% for non-behavioral infra changes.
- Canary duration floor: 30 minutes at initial weight, then staged doubling every 30–60 minutes conditional on green signals.
- Synthetic smoke test pass: end-to-end test suite (latency, correctness, retry behavior) must pass on canary cluster.
- Dependency freeze window: no infra changes 1 hour before scheduled activation.

Telemetry checklist (dashboard essentials):
- Route-level p50/p95/p99, error rate, timeouts, retries.
- Control vs experiment comparison panels (latency and correctness).
- Token cost per request and aggregated spend rate.
- Sampled outputs log (random 1 in 1k) with prompt and metadata.
- Canary control chart with automated anomaly detection markers.

Pre-launch dry-run checklist (tick boxes):
- [ ] Activation owner assigned and on calendar.
- [ ] Runbook link shared with oncall and CS.
- [ ] Synthetic traffic smoke test green on canary nodes.
- [ ] Dashboards and alert thresholds deployed to canary channel.
- [ ] Backout/fallback variant validated and stored as config.
- [ ] Post-activation review slot reserved (30–60m) on owner's calendar.

Small experiments operational notes (practical tips):
- Prefer more short canaries rather than one long ramp when uncertainty is behavioral.
- Use orthogonal slices (region, client tier) to avoid confounding signals.
- Seed synthetic requests for low-traffic cohorts to accelerate signal detection while being cautious about biasing metrics.

Open questions / items to resolve in follow-ups:
- Who is authorized to flip an automatic fallback for enterprise-provisioned Dedicated customers? (policy needed)
- Should token-cost delta be per-route or account-aggregated for guard triggering?
- Define severity classification mapping for combined signal failures (latency + sem-regression).

Next steps (near term):
- Iterate on thresholds after 3 production canaries (owner: Observability Lead).
- Run tabletop drill with SRE, CS, and product for the de-escalation playbook (owner: Activation Lead).
- Draft a short owner cheat sheet (1 pager) and pin to canary-ops Slack.

Historical artifacts and references:
- See linked confluence page (CONFLUENCE-1234) for background theory and earlier experiments.
- Simulation repo: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-simulations (PR linked above).

Notes to self: keep this doc tightly actionable. Avoid over-generalizing; prefer clear thresholds and single-person ownership for fast decisions.

END WIP
